text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BCN WANTS BANERJ; BOSTON WANTS CREDIREAL

Brazilian bank BCN has presented the necessary documents to prequalify for the privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, while other already prequalified banks have lost interest in Banerj, like Bank of Boston which prefers Credireal.
-- ECONOMY SENDS CONFLICTING SIGNALS
Central Bank Monetary Policy Director Francisco Lopes said it would take another two months before economic indicators could give a clear picture on the extent of heating up of the economy.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- POLICE ARRESTS MAFIOSO LINKED TO EX-COLLOR AIDE FARIAS

Brazilian federal police have arrested Domenico Verde, an Italian mafioso with Brazilian citizenship who is wanted by the Italian government and suspected of money laundering ties with the late Paulo Cesar Faria, the former aide of ex-president Fernando Collor.
-- TEACHER FORCES STUDENT TO WEAR SKIRT AS PUNISHMENT
A math teacher in Rio de Janeiro is being sued because he made one of his male pupils wear a skirt to punish him for cheating during an exam.
O GLOBO
-- NEW SYSTEM WILL CUT INTEREST FOR HOME BUYERS 13 PERCENT
The government wants to introduce a new type of bank loan to finance home buyers which would bring interest rates down to 13 percent from the current 18 percent.
-- SOCCER COACH KILLED IN SHANTYTOWN
A children's soccer coach was shot dead accidentily in a Rio de Janeiro shantytown by drug traffickers who aimed at a rival who was standing next to the coach.
-- BRAZIL BONDS RISE 0.75 PCT IN ONE DAY
One day after the successful launch of Brazilian Treasury bonds worth $3 billion the bonds gained 0.75 percent in value.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
